question:
What is the standard Japanese pitch accent pattern of 「弟」?

Answer Choices:
A. Heiban
B. Atamadaka
C. Nakadaka
D. Odaka
E. Heiban or Nakadaka

2.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I believe the answer is E. Heiban or Nakadaka. 「弟」 is pronounced おとうと, and in many standard dictionaries the default is listed as a relatively flat or mildly rising pattern without a clear early drop (heiban-like), while some speakers or regional variants place a slight peak on the second mora before leveling (nakadaka). This variability seems common for kinship terms of this length, so both patterns are attested rather than a single fixed accent.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The word 「弟」 (otōto) consists of four moras (お-とう-と). Its standard Tokyo pitch accent is L-H-H-L. This places the pitch drop after the third mora, which matches the definition of nakadaka (C). It is therefore not heiban (which would stay high through the end), not atamadaka (which drops immediately after the first mora), and not odaka (which would be high on the final mora and only drop before a following particle). 

(The same pattern applies to the near-synonym 妹 imōto.)

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. Heiban

The word 「弟」 (おとうと) consists of three moras (o-tō-to). In standard Tokyo Japanese, it follows the heiban pattern: an initial low pitch on the first mora followed by a rise that remains high and level through the end of the word (LHH), with no pitch drop even when a particle is added. This matches the accent of other common heiban family terms such as 兄 (あに). It is distinct from the nakadaka pattern of 妹 (いもうと).
